title: Castleridge Labs — BizDev jotter: outbound angles & objections
content:
Quick sketch for Castleridge Labs outreach (biotech data platform) — raw notes.

Context:
- Castleridge Labs: mid-market bioinformatics + SaaS for lab workflow automation. ~120 employees. Heavy on sensitive PII / research IP. CTO = Aaron Lin, Head of Data Infrastructure = Priyanka Singh (likely champion).
- From research: run inference for document summarization, experiment-note search, and SOP generation. They currently use an in-house fine-tuned model (costly), considering vendor APIs. Strong constraint: must be on VPC/private (security + compliance).

Hypothesis / Value props to test:
- Private deployment (on-prem/VPC) + single API across hosted/dedicated: removes lift for their infra team.
- Cost predictability vs current fine-tune + in-house serving. Present a model: projected 40% lower per-token cost with batching + KV cache for experiment notes reuse.
- Observability: lineage for prompts and evals to satisfy audit requests (R&D compliance).

Key personas to target (sequence plan):
1) Priyanka Singh — Head of Data Infrastructure (technical champion): pain = ops overhead, unpredictable latency during spikes.
2) Aaron Lin — CTO (economic + security): needs SLA + private control plane for IP protection.
3) Sarah Delgado — Head of R&D Ops / Compliance (regulatory angle): needs auditability, KMS/HSM integration.

Outbound subject line A/Bs (for email sequences):
A: Quick note — private LLM inference for Castleridge experiment notes
B: Lowering inference ops cost for Priyanka (VPC-ready)
C: Audit-friendly model serving? Short call?

Short cold email (30–40 words) — tech-first, for Priyanka:
Hi Priyanka — Elena from Redwood Inference. We help infra teams replace brittle in-house serving with a VPC-capable runtime that keeps tokens private, reduces per-token spend, and guarantees latency SLOs. 10–15min to see whether this maps to your backlog?

Follow-up (if no response) — offer value:
- Offer a small profiling run: 24–48h inference cost/latency snapshot on a representative prompt set (we run on dedicated backed environment or point them to pilot kit).

Call script highlights (intro to Priyanka):
- 2 min: quick intro + what other bio customers solved with us (no names).
- 5 min: ask about current serving architecture, model sizes, and peak qps.
- 5 min: discuss SLOs they're missing and security reqs (KMS, VPC).
- 3 min: propose next step — PoC: 2-week private pilot on a dedicated node group, Redwood handles model onboarding and perf tuning.

Objections & suggested rebuttals (brief):
1) Objection: "We can't send research data to external services."
   - Rebuttal: Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) + optional on-prem package. KMS/HSM integration means keys never leave customer boundary. Share architecture whitepaper + network diagram.
2) Objection: "We already fine-tuned a model; moving will regress quality."
   - Rebuttal: Support model pinning and rollout; we can do canary traffic split and A/B evals on your test prompts to measure quality delta before you switch. Offer automated eval harness.
3) Objection: "Cost uncertain / vendor lock-in concerns."
   - Rebuttal: Show transparent per-token breakdown, batching/quantization levers in Optimize that reduce unit cost. Contract terms for Dedicated include predictable capacity pricing; can include exit data export clauses.
4) Objection: "We're too small for a Dedicated contract."
   - Rebuttal: Start with a short Private pilot (timeboxed) or hosted trial with strict privacy controls to prove ROI, then scale to Dedicated.

Technical checklist to prep before PoC:
- Sample prompt set (50–200 representative prompts across SDR, SOPs, experiment notes).
- Current model sizes + token distribution (median seq len, 95th pct).
- Peak requests/sec and concurrency targets.
- Security matrix: required certifications, KMS provider, approved IP flows.

Metrics to promise / measure during PoC:
- 95th pct latency under target (e.g., <300ms for generation baseline)
- Per-token cost delta vs baseline (show absolute and %)
- Error/regression rate on evaluators (automated prompt set)
- Uptime/availability for test window

Email template — CEO/CTO touch (short, strategic):
Subject: Protecting Castleridge IP while cutting inference ops cost
Hi Aaron — saw Castleridge's recent paper on pipeline automation. We’ve helped infra leaders cut inference unit costs and run private, auditable deployments for sensitive workloads. If you care about predictable spend + retaining IP control, I can share a two-page brief and a sketch of a 2-week pilot. Interested?

Notes to self / tactical things to do:
- Ask Marcus to pull sample token distribution from any public runs we used with similar customers.
- Prep 1-page network diagram for Private (show KMS + VPC peering patterns).
- Quick internal ask: legal to draft a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) template for pilot customers with IP protections.
- Add Sarah (solutions eng) to next call — she can speak to audit/logging and rollout options.

Competitive signals to watch for in discovery:
- If they mention huggingface or AWS Bedrock pilots: price/time-to-integration angle.
- If they mention building more in-house: highlight maintenance burden + kernel/serving ops complexity.

Potential pilot offer (sticky, low-friction):
- 2-week Private pilot: Redwood sets up a dedicated node pool in their VPC (or on-prem package), we run a pre-agreed prompt set. Deliverables: cost/latency report, evaluation dashboard, and a migration playbook.
- Success criteria: 20%+ cost reduction OR sub-300ms median latency for top 3 workflows AND no data leaving customer perimeter.

Next actions (this week):
- Email Priyanka (cold A) + put follow-up task in sequence (day 3, day 7).
- Assemble pilot brief + network diagram (Sofia).
- Internal: get legal note from Maria on DPA variations for research IP.

Random brain dump / angles to test in calls:
- Ask about audit trails for model inference — tie to regulatory audits they might face.
- Pitch the idea of a "read-only" pilot: Redwood cannot write model artifacts to their storage; only read inference logs for metrics (mitigate IP concerns).
- Offer to run a short economic model showing TCO of maintaining their current fine-tune pipeline vs Redwood-managed serving.

End of jotter. Keep it lean — use as script for first 2 calls.

-- Elena
